title: Topology evidence provenance with SHA256 bindings

defect_summary.topology_certification_no_bindings: certify_topology() returned SPEC_TOPOLOGY/RECOVERY_DIAGNOSTIC statuses but included no SHA256 of the input summaries (literal/recovered) or the certification result itself. A swapped or tampered summary could not be detected.
defect_summary.map_acceptance_no_artifact_hashes: build_map_acceptance() included linked_artifacts paths but not their SHA256 hashes, so artifact substitution was undetectable. The acceptance payload itself had no self-hash or provenance.
defect_summary.no_provenance: Neither tool included tool version, git SHA, or environment metadata, preventing forensic traceability.
defect_summary.no_schema_version: Outputs lacked a versioned schema identifier, making forward/backward compatibility fragile.

corrected_semantics.topology_certification: certify_topology() returns schema v1 with input_bindings (literal_summary_sha256, recovered_summary_sha256), certification_sha256 (self-hash), and provenance block (tool, git SHA, Python version). Schema v1 enables forward compatibility.
corrected_semantics.map_acceptance: build_map_acceptance() returns schema v1 with linked_artifact_sha256 (SHA256 of every linked artifact), acceptance_artifact_sha256, payload_sha256 (self-hash), and provenance block (tool, git SHA, Python version). Schema v1 enables forward compatibility.
corrected_semantics.both_tools: Both tools now include a provenance block (tool name, git SHA, Python version) and schema version for forensic traceability and forward compatibility.

tests.coverage: All existing tests for topology_certification (literal/recovered graphs, flipped contactPoint, waiver logic, missing evidence) and map_acceptance (all gates, enrichment, waiver, semantic completeness, component reachability) pass without modification.

residual_risks: Input summaries to certify_topology must be deterministic JSON-serializable objects for SHA256 to be stable; non-deterministic field ordering would break bindings.
Git SHA capture depends on git being available; falls back to empty string if unavailable.

The linked_artifact_sha256 in map_acceptance only covers artifacts that exist at acceptance time; if an artifact is deleted between gate execution and acceptance, its hash is missing (recorded as absent).
Certification result SHA256 excludes the certification_sha256 field itself (circular reference), which is standard but must be documented for verifiers.
